node.label: Employment & labour codes
node.summary: PLFS data, the Decent Work Index, informal employment and the four Labour Codes.

facts.text: PLFS data show India's unemployment rate fell from **6.1% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24)**, but a Decent Work Index (DWI) rose only from 0.247 to 0.302 over the same period; nearly 90% of the workforce remains informally employed (India Employment Report 2024, ILO-IHD), and agriculture's DWI (0.211→0.267) stayed the lowest despite four Labour Codes notified in 2025.

facts.text: The **four Labour Codes** (Wages 2019; Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions 2020) came into force on **21 Nov 2025**, replacing 29 central labour laws.
facts.plain: The four Labour Codes (Wages 2019; Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions 2020) came into force on 21 Nov 2025, replacing 29 central labour laws.

facts.text: The editorial says the boards are too centralised: labour is in the **Concurrent List**; unorganised and gig workers are over **92%** of the workforce; the government claims social security coverage rose from **19% (2015) to 64.3% (2025)**. The **NCEUS** (chaired by **Arjun Sengupta**) had made recommendations two decades ago.

facts.text: One year after the **Code on Social Security**, the Labour Ministry notified two boards chaired by Minister **Mansukh Mandaviya**: the **National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers (40 members)** and for **Gig & Platform Workers (22 members)**; they meet at least thrice a year. Members include Eternal (Zomato), Swiggy, Zepto, Urban Company and Rapido.
